1| """
2| The logic in this module builds a portion of a WHERE SQL
3| clause based on a SCIM filter.
4| """
5| import ast
6| import string
7| 
8| from .. import ast as scim2ast
9| 
10| 
11| class Transpiler(ast.NodeTransformer):
12|     """
13|     Transpile a SCIM AST into a SQL WHERE clause (not including the "WHERE" keyword)
14|     """
15| 
16|     def __init__(self, attr_map, *args, **kwargs):
17|         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
18| 
19|         self.attr_map = attr_map
20|         self.params = {}
21|         self.attr_paths = []
22| 
23|     def transpile(self, ast) -> (str, dict):
24|         sql = self.visit(ast)
25| 
26|         return sql, self.params
27| 
28|     def visit_Filter(self, node):
29|         if node.namespace:
30|             # push the namespace from value path down the tree
31|             if isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.Filter):
32|                 node.expr = scim2ast.Filter(node.expr.expr, node.expr.negated, node.namespace)
33|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.LogExpr):
34|                 expr1 = scim2ast.Filter(node.expr.expr1.expr, node.expr.expr1.negated, node.namespace)
35|                 expr2 = scim2ast.Filter(node.expr.expr2.expr, node.expr.expr2.negated, node.namespace)
36|                 node.expr = scim2ast.LogExpr(node.expr.op, expr1, expr2)
37|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.AttrExpr):
38|                 # namespace takes place of previous attr_name in attr_path
39|                 sub_attr = scim2ast.SubAttr(node.expr.attr_path.attr_name)
40|                 attr_path = scim2ast.AttrPath(node.namespace.attr_name, sub_attr, node.expr.attr_path.uri)
41|                 node.expr = scim2ast.AttrExpr(node.expr.value, attr_path, node.expr.comp_value)
42|             else:
43|                 raise NotImplementedError(f'Node {node} can not pass on namespace')
44| 
45|         expr = self.visit(node.expr)
46| 
47|         if expr and node.negated:
48|             expr = f'NOT ({expr})'
49| 
50|         return expr
51| 
52|     def visit_LogExpr(self, node):
53|         expr1 = self.visit(node.expr1)
54|         expr2 = self.visit(node.expr2)
55|         op = node.op.upper()
56| 
57|         if expr1 and expr2:
58|             return f'({expr1}) {op} ({expr2})'
59|         elif expr1:
60|             return expr1
61|         elif expr2:
62|             return expr2
63|         else:
64|             return None
65| 
66|     def visit_PartialAttrExpr(self, node):
67|         """
68|         Dissect rather complex queries like the following::
69| 
70|             emails[type eq "Primary"].value eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
71| 
72|         First we restructure to something like this::
73| 
74|             emails.value[type eq "Primary"] eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
75| 
76|         Then we get SQL like this 'emails.type = {0}' and 'emails.value'.
77| 
78|         We need to take these two snippets and AND them together.
79|         """
80|         # visit full filter first and restructure AST
81|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.type = {0}'
82|         full = self.visit(node)
83| 
84|         # get second part of query
85|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.value'
86|         partial = self.visit(node.namespace)
87| 
88|         return full, partial
89| 
90|     def visit_AttrExpr(self, node):
91|         if isinstance(node.attr_path.attr_name, scim2ast.Filter):
92|             full, partial = self.visit_PartialAttrExpr(node.attr_path.attr_name)
93|             if full and partial:
94|                 value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
95|                 return f'({full} AND {partial} {value})'
96|             elif full:
97|                 return full
98|             elif partial:
99|                 value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
100|                 return f'{partial} {value}'
101|             else:
102|                 return None
103|         else:
104|             attr = self.visit(node.attr_path)
105|             if attr is None:
106|                 return None
107|             value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
108|             return f'{attr} {value}'
109| 
110|     def visit_AttrExprValue(self, node_value, node_comp_value):
111|         op_sql = self.lookup_op(node_value)
112| 
113|         item_id = self.get_next_id()
114| 
115|         if not node_comp_value:
116|             self.params[item_id] = None
117|             return op_sql
118| 
119|         # There is a comp_value, so visit node and build SQL.
120| 
121|         # prep item_id to be a str replacement placeholder
122|         item_id_placeholder = '{' + item_id + '}'
123| 
124|         if 'LIKE' == op_sql:
125|             # Add appropriate % signs to values in LIKE clause
126|             prefix, suffix = self.lookup_like_matching(node_value)
127|             value = prefix + self.visit(node_comp_value) + suffix
128|         else:
129|             value = self.visit(node_comp_value)
130| 
131|         self.params[item_id] = value
132| 
133|         return f'{op_sql} {item_id_placeholder}'
134| 
135|     def visit_AttrPath(self, node):
136|         attr_name_value = node.attr_name
137| 
138|         sub_attr_value = None
139|         if node.sub_attr:
140|             sub_attr_value = node.sub_attr.value
141| 
142|         uri_value = None
143|         if node.uri:
144|             uri_value = node.uri
145|

1| '''
2| This file defines classes for different kinds of nodes of an Abstract
3| Syntax Tree. In general, you will have a different AST node for
4| each kind of grammar rule.
5| 
6| This file has a small bit of metaprogramming to simplify specification
7| and to perform some validation steps.
8| '''
9| 
10| 
11| class AST(object):
12|     _nodes = {}
13| 
14|     @classmethod
15|     def __init_subclass__(cls):
16|         AST._nodes[cls.__name__] = cls
17| 
18|         if not hasattr(cls, '__annotations__'):
19|             return
20| 
21|         cls._fields = list(cls.__annotations__)
22| 
23|     def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
24|         if len(args) != len(self._fields):
25|             raise TypeError(f'{str(self)}: Expected {len(self._fields)} arguments')
26| 
27|         for name, val in zip(self._fields, args):
28|             setattr(self, name, val)
29| 
30|         for name, val in kwargs.items():
31|             setattr(self, name, val)
32| 
33|     def __repr__(self):
34|         parts = []
35| 
36|         for name in self._fields:
37|             val = getattr(self, name)
38| 
39|             if isinstance(val, AST):
40|                 parts.append(f'{name}={type(val).__name__}')
41| 
42|             elif isinstance(val, list):
43|                 parts.append(f'{name}=[ len={len(val)} ]')
44| 
45|             else:
46|                 parts.append(f'{name}={repr(val)}')
47| 
48|         argstr = ', '.join(parts)
49| 
50|         return f'{type(self).__name__}({argstr})'
51|

53| # Specific AST nodes.
54| #
55| # For each of these nodes, you need to add type annotations that
56| # specify which fields are to be stored.  Just as an example, for a
57| # binary operator, you might store the operator, the left expression,
58| # and the right expression like this:

61| #          pass
62| #

64| #          op : str
65| #          left : Expression
66| #          right : Expression
67| #

69| # any effect on the underlying operation.
70| #

74| # classes inherit from them.

77| class Filter(AST):
78|     expr      : AST  # noqa: E203
79|     negated   : bool  # noqa: E203
80|     namespace : AST  # noqa: E203

86|     expr2 : Filter  # noqa: E203

109| # The following classes for visiting and rewriting the AST are taken
110| # from Python's ast module.   It's really easy to make mistakes when
111| # naming methods in visitor classes so there's a bit of metaprogramming
112| # to make sure we're not writing duplicate definitions and to make
113| # sure methods match up with the names of actual AST nodes.
114| 
115| class VisitDict(dict):
116|     def __setitem__(self, key, value):
117|         if key in self:
118|             raise AttributeError(f'Duplicate definition for {key}')
119|         super().__setitem__(key, value)
120| 
121| 
122| class NodeVisitMeta(type):
123|     @classmethod
124|     def __prepare__(cls, name, bases):
125|         return VisitDict()

127| 
128| class NodeVisitor(metaclass=NodeVisitMeta):
129|     '''
130|     Class for visiting nodes of the parse tree.  This is modeled after
131|     a similar class in the standard library ast.NodeVisitor.  For each
132|     node, the visit(node) method calls a method visit_NodeName(node)
133|     which should be implemented in subclasses.  The generic_visit() method
134|     is called for all nodes where there is no matching visit_NodeName() method.
135| 
136|     Here is a example of a visitor that examines binary operators::
137| 
138|         class VisitOps(NodeVisitor):
139|             visit_BinOp(self,node):

141|                 self.visit(node.left)
142|                 self.visit(node.right)
143|             visit_UnaryOp(self,node):

153|         NodeName is the name of the class of a particular node.

166|         This examines the node to see if it has `_fields`, is a list,

185|     Flatten the entire parse tree into a list for the purposes of
186|     debugging and testing.  This returns a list of tuples of the
187|     form (depth, node) where depth is an integer representing the
188|     parse tree depth and node is the associated AST node.

96|     def visit_PartialAttrExpr(self, node):
97|         """
98|         Dissect rather complex queries like the following::
99| 
100|             emails[type eq "Primary"].value eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
101| 
102|         First we restructure to something like this::
103| 
104|             emails.value[type eq "Primary"] eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
105| 
106|         Then we get SQL like this 'emails.type = {0}' and 'emails.value'.
107| 
108|         We need to take these two snippets and AND them together.
109|         """
110|         # visit full filter first and restructure AST
111|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.type = {0}'
112|         full = self.visit(node)
113| 
114|         # get second part of query
115|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.value'
116|         partial = self.visit(node.namespace)
117|         return full, partial
118| 
119|     def is_filter(self, node):
120|         full, partial = self.visit_PartialAttrExpr(node.attr_path.attr_name)
121|         if partial and "." in partial:
122|             partial = partial.replace(".", "__")
123|         if full and partial:
124|             # Specific to Azure
125|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
126|             key = partial + "__" + op
127|             return full & Q(**{key: value})
128|         elif full:
129|             return full
130|         elif partial:
131|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
132|             key = partial + "__" + op
133|             return Q(**{key: value})
134|         else:
135|             return None
136| 
137|     def visit_AttrExpr(self, node):
138|         if isinstance(node.attr_path.attr_name, scim2ast.Filter):
139|             return self.is_filter(node)
140|         attr = self.visit(node.attr_path)
141|         if attr is None:
142|             return None
143|         if "." in attr:
144|             attr = attr.replace(".", "__")
145|         op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
146|         key = attr + "__" + op
147|         query = Q(**{key: value})
148|         if node.value == "ne":
149|             query = ~query
150|         return query
151| 
152|     def visit_AttrExprValue(self, node_value, node_comp_value):
153|         op = self.lookup_op(node_value)
154| 
155|         if node_comp_value:
156|             # There is a comp_value, so visit node and build SQL.
157|             # prep item_id to be a str replacement placeholder
158|             value = self.visit(node_comp_value)
159|         else:
160|             value = None
161| 
162|         if op == "isnull":  # __isnull=False
163|             value = False
164| 
165|         return op, value
166| 
167|     def visit_AttrPath(self, node):
168|         attr_name_value = node.attr_name.lower()
169|         sub_attr_value = None
170|         if node.sub_attr:
171|             sub_attr_value = node.sub_attr.value.lower()
172| 
173|         uri_value = None
174|         if node.uri:
175|             uri_value = node.uri.lower()
176| 
177|         # Convert attr_name to another value based on map.
178|         # Otherwise, return None.
179|         attr_path_tuple = (attr_name_value, sub_attr_value, uri_value)
180|         return self.attr_map.get(attr_path_tuple)
181| 
182|     @staticmethod
183|     def visit_CompValue(node):
184|         if node.value == "true":
185|             return True
186|         elif node.value == "false":
187|             return False
188|         elif node.value == "null":
189|             return None
190|         else:
191|             return node.value
192| 
193|     @staticmethod
194|     def lookup_op(node_value):
195|         op_code = node_value.lower()
196| 
197|         op = {
198|             "eq": "iexact",
199|             "ne": "iexact",
200|             "co": "icontains",
201|             "sw": "istartswith",
202|             "ew": "iendswith",
203|             "pr": "isnull",
204|             "gt": "gt",
205|             "ge": "gte",
206|             "lt": "lt",
207|             "le": "lte",
208|         }.get(op_code)
209| 
210|         if not op:
211|             raise ValueError(f"Unknown Django op {op_code}")
212| 
213|         return op or node_value

1| """
2| The logic in this module builds a Django Q object from an SCIM filter.
3| """
4| import ast
5| from typing import Mapping
6| 
7| from django.db.models import Q
8| 
9| from scim2_filter_parser import ast as scim2ast
10| from scim2_filter_parser.lexer import SCIMLexer
11| from scim2_filter_parser.parser import SCIMParser
12| 
13| 
14| def get_query(scim_query: str, attr_map: Mapping):
15|     token_stream = SCIMLexer().tokenize(scim_query)
16|     tree = SCIMParser().parse(token_stream)
17|     return Transpiler(attr_map).transpile(tree)
18| 
19| 
20| def attr_map_with_lower_keys(attr_map: Mapping) -> Mapping:
21|     attr_map_lower_case = {}
22|     for (a, b, c), v in attr_map.items():
23|         if a:
24|             a = a.lower()
25|         if b:
26|             b = b.lower()
27|         if c:
28|             c = c.lower()
29|         attr_map_lower_case[(a, b, c)] = v
30|     return attr_map_lower_case
31| 
32| 
33| # noinspection PyPep8Naming
34| class Transpiler(ast.NodeTransformer):
35|     """
36|     Transpile a SCIM AST into a Q object
37|     """
38| 
39|     def __init__(self, attr_map: Mapping, *args, **kwargs):
40|         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
41|         self.attr_map = attr_map_with_lower_keys(attr_map)
42| 
43|     def transpile(self, scim_ast) -> (str, dict):
44|         return self.visit(scim_ast)
45| 
46|     def visit_Filter(self, node):
47|         if node.namespace:
48|             # push the namespace from value path down the tree
49|             if isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.Filter):
50|                 node.expr = scim2ast.Filter(
51|                     node.expr.expr, node.expr.negated, node.namespace
52|                 )
53|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.LogExpr):
54|                 expr1 = scim2ast.Filter(
55|                     node.expr.expr1.expr, node.expr.expr1.negated, node.namespace
56|                 )
57|                 expr2 = scim2ast.Filter(
58|                     node.expr.expr2.expr, node.expr.expr2.negated, node.namespace
59|                 )
60|                 node.expr = scim2ast.LogExpr(node.expr.op, expr1, expr2)
61|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.AttrExpr):
62|                 # namespace takes place of previous attr_name in attr_path
63|                 sub_attr = scim2ast.SubAttr(node.expr.attr_path.attr_name)
64|                 attr_path = scim2ast.AttrPath(
65|                     node.namespace.attr_name, sub_attr, node.expr.attr_path.uri
66|                 )
67|                 node.expr = scim2ast.AttrExpr(
68|                     node.expr.value, attr_path, node.expr.comp_value
69|                 )
70|             else:
71|                 raise NotImplementedError(f"Node {node} can not pass on namespace")
72| 
73|         query = self.visit(node.expr)
74| 
75|         if query and node.negated:
76|             query = ~query
77| 
78|         return query
79| 
80|     def visit_LogExpr(self, node):
81|         q1 = self.visit(node.expr1)
82|         q2 = self.visit(node.expr2)
83|         op = node.op.upper()
84|         if q1 and q2:
85|             if op == "AND":
86|                 return q1 & q2
87|             elif op == "OR":
88|                 return q1 | q2
89|         elif q1:
90|             return q1
91|         elif q2:
92|             return q2
93|         else:
94|             return None
95| 
96|     def visit_PartialAttrExpr(self, node):
97|         """
98|         Dissect rather complex queries like the following::
99| 
100|             emails[type eq "Primary"].value eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
101| 
102|         First we restructure to something like this::
103| 
104|             emails.value[type eq "Primary"] eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
105| 
106|         Then we get SQL like this 'emails.type = {0}' and 'emails.value'.
107| 
108|         We need to take these two snippets and AND them together.
109|         """
110|         # visit full filter first and restructure AST
111|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.type = {0}'
112|         full = self.visit(node)
113| 
114|         # get second part of query
115|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.value'
116|         partial = self.visit(node.namespace)
117|         return full, partial
118| 
119|     def is_filter(self, node):
120|         full, partial = self.visit_PartialAttrExpr(node.attr_path.attr_name)
121|         if partial and "." in partial:
122|             partial = partial.replace(".", "__")
123|         if full and partial:
124|             # Specific to Azure
125|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
126|             key = partial + "__" + op
127|             return full & Q(**{key: value})
128|         elif full:
129|             return full
130|         elif partial:
131|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
132|             key = partial + "__" + op
133|             return Q(**{key: value})
134|         else:
135|             return None
136| 
137|     def visit_AttrExpr(self, node):
138|         if isinstance(node.attr_path.attr_name, scim2ast.Filter):
139|             return self.is_filter(node)
140|         attr = self.visit(node.attr_path)
141|         if attr is None:
142|             return None
143|         if "." in attr:
144|             attr = attr.replace(".", "__")
145|         op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
146|         key = attr + "__" + op
147|         query = Q(**{key: value})
148|         if node.value == "ne":
149|             query = ~query
150|         return query
151| 
152|     def visit_AttrExprValue(self, node_value, node_comp_value):
153|         op = self.lookup_op(node_value)
154| 
155|         if node_comp_value:
156|             # There is a comp_value, so visit node and build SQL.
157|             # prep item_id to be a str replacement placeholder
158|             value = self.visit(node_comp_value)
159|         else:
160|             value = None
161| 
162|         if op == "isnull":  # __isnull=False
163|             value = False
164| 
165|         return op, value
166| 
167|     def visit_AttrPath(self, node):
168|         attr_name_value = node.attr_name.lower()
169|         sub_attr_value = None
170|         if node.sub_attr:
171|             sub_attr_value = node.sub_attr.value.lower()
172| 
173|         uri_value = None
174|         if node.uri:
175|             uri_value = node.uri.lower()
176| 
177|         # Convert attr_name to another value based on map.
178|         # Otherwise, return None.
179|         attr_path_tuple = (attr_name_value, sub_attr_value, uri_value)
180|         return self.attr_map.get(attr_path_tuple)
181| 
182|     @staticmethod
183|     def visit_CompValue(node):
184|         if node.value == "true":
185|             return True
186|         elif node.value == "false":
187|             return False
188|         elif node.value == "null":
189|             return None
190|         else:
191|             return node.value
192| 
193|     @staticmethod
194|     def lookup_op(node_value):
195|         op_code = node_value.lower()
196| 
197|         op = {
198|             "eq": "iexact",
199|             "ne": "iexact",
200|             "co": "icontains",
201|             "sw": "istartswith",
202|             "ew": "iendswith",
203|             "pr": "isnull",
204|             "gt": "gt",
205|             "ge": "gte",
206|             "lt": "lt",
207|             "le": "lte",
208|         }.get(op_code)
209| 
210|         if not op:
211|             raise ValueError(f"Unknown Django op {op_code}")
212| 
213|         return op or node_value

2| The logic in this module builds a Django Q object from an SCIM filter.

4| import ast
5| from typing import Mapping
6| 
7| from django.db.models import Q
8| 
9| from scim2_filter_parser import ast as scim2ast
10| from scim2_filter_parser.lexer import SCIMLexer
11| from scim2_filter_parser.parser import SCIMParser
12| 
13| 
14| def get_query(scim_query: str, attr_map: Mapping):
15|     token_stream = SCIMLexer().tokenize(scim_query)
16|     tree = SCIMParser().parse(token_stream)
17|     return Transpiler(attr_map).transpile(tree)
18| 
19| 
20| def attr_map_with_lower_keys(attr_map: Mapping) -> Mapping:
21|     attr_map_lower_case = {}
22|     for (a, b, c), v in attr_map.items():
23|         if a:
24|             a = a.lower()
25|         if b:
26|             b = b.lower()
27|         if c:
28|             c = c.lower()
29|         attr_map_lower_case[(a, b, c)] = v
30|     return attr_map_lower_case
31| 
32| 
33| # noinspection PyPep8Naming
34| class Transpiler(ast.NodeTransformer):
35|     """
36|     Transpile a SCIM AST into a Q object
37|     """
38| 
39|     def __init__(self, attr_map: Mapping, *args, **kwargs):
40|         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
41|         self.attr_map = attr_map_with_lower_keys(attr_map)
42| 
43|     def transpile(self, scim_ast) -> (str, dict):
44|         return self.visit(scim_ast)
45| 
46|     def visit_Filter(self, node):
47|         if node.namespace:
48|             # push the namespace from value path down the tree
49|             if isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.Filter):
50|                 node.expr = scim2ast.Filter(
51|                     node.expr.expr, node.expr.negated, node.namespace
52|                 )
53|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.LogExpr):
54|                 expr1 = scim2ast.Filter(
55|                     node.expr.expr1.expr, node.expr.expr1.negated, node.namespace
56|                 )
57|                 expr2 = scim2ast.Filter(
58|                     node.expr.expr2.expr, node.expr.expr2.negated, node.namespace
59|                 )
60|                 node.expr = scim2ast.LogExpr(node.expr.op, expr1, expr2)
61|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.AttrExpr):
62|                 # namespace takes place of previous attr_name in attr_path
63|                 sub_attr = scim2ast.SubAttr(node.expr.attr_path.attr_name)
64|                 attr_path = scim2ast.AttrPath(
65|                     node.namespace.attr_name, sub_attr, node.expr.attr_path.uri
66|                 )
67|                 node.expr = scim2ast.AttrExpr(
68|                     node.expr.value, attr_path, node.expr.comp_value
69|                 )
70|             else:
71|                 raise NotImplementedError(f"Node {node} can not pass on namespace")
72| 
73|         query = self.visit(node.expr)
74| 
75|         if query and node.negated:
76|             query = ~query
77| 
78|         return query
79| 
80|     def visit_LogExpr(self, node):
81|         q1 = self.visit(node.expr1)
82|         q2 = self.visit(node.expr2)
83|         op = node.op.upper()
84|         if q1 and q2:
85|             if op == "AND":
86|                 return q1 & q2
87|             elif op == "OR":
88|                 return q1 | q2
89|         elif q1:
90|             return q1
91|         elif q2:
92|             return q2
93|         else:
94|             return None
95| 
96|     def visit_PartialAttrExpr(self, node):
97|         """
98|         Dissect rather complex queries like the following::
99| 
100|             emails[type eq "Primary"].value eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
101| 
102|         First we restructure to something like this::
103| 
104|             emails.value[type eq "Primary"] eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
105| 
106|         Then we get SQL like this 'emails.type = {0}' and 'emails.value'.
107| 
108|         We need to take these two snippets and AND them together.
109|         """
110|         # visit full filter first and restructure AST
111|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.type = {0}'
112|         full = self.visit(node)
113| 
114|         # get second part of query
115|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.value'
116|         partial = self.visit(node.namespace)
117|         return full, partial
118| 
119|     def is_filter(self, node):
120|         full, partial = self.visit_PartialAttrExpr(node.attr_path.attr_name)
121|         if partial and "." in partial:
122|             partial = partial.replace(".", "__")
123|         if full and partial:
124|             # Specific to Azure
125|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
126|             key = partial + "__" + op
127|             return full & Q(**{key: value})
128|         elif full:
129|             return full
130|         elif partial:
131|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
132|             key = partial + "__" + op
133|             return Q(**{key: value})
134|         else:
135|             return None
136| 
137|     def visit_AttrExpr(self, node):
138|         if isinstance(node.attr_path.attr_name, scim2ast.Filter):
139|             return self.is_filter(node)
140|         attr = self.visit(node.attr_path)
141|         if attr is None:
142|             return None
143|         if "." in attr:
144|             attr = attr.replace(".", "__")
145|         op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
146|         key = attr + "__" + op
147|         query = Q(**{key: value})
148|         if node.value == "ne":
149|             query = ~query
150|         return query
151| 
152|     def visit_AttrExprValue(self, node_value, node_comp_value):
153|         op = self.lookup_op(node_value)
154| 
155|         if node_comp_value:
156|             # There is a comp_value, so visit node and build SQL.
157|             # prep item_id to be a str replacement placeholder
158|             value = self.visit(node_comp_value)
159|         else:
160|             value = None
161| 
162|         if op == "isnull":  # __isnull=False
163|             value = False
164| 
165|         return op, value
166| 
167|     def visit_AttrPath(self, node):
168|         attr_name_value = node.attr_name.lower()
169|         sub_attr_value = None
170|         if node.sub_attr:
171|             sub_attr_value = node.sub_attr.value.lower()
172| 
173|         uri_value = None
174|         if node.uri:
175|             uri_value = node.uri.lower()
176| 
177|         # Convert attr_name to another value based on map.
178|         # Otherwise, return None.
179|         attr_path_tuple = (attr_name_value, sub_attr_value, uri_value)
180|         return self.attr_map.get(attr_path_tuple)
181| 
182|     @staticmethod
183|     def visit_CompValue(node):
184|         if node.value == "true":
185|             return True
186|         elif node.value == "false":
187|             return False
188|         elif node.value == "null":
189|             return None
190|         else:
191|             return node.value
192| 
193|     @staticmethod
194|     def lookup_op(node_value):
195|         op_code = node_value.lower()
196| 
197|         op = {
198|             "eq": "iexact",
199|             "ne": "iexact",
200|             "co": "icontains",
201|             "sw": "istartswith",
202|             "ew": "iendswith",
203|             "pr": "isnull",
204|             "gt": "gt",
205|             "ge": "gte",
206|             "lt": "lt",
207|             "le": "lte",
208|         }.get(op_code)
209| 
210|         if not op:
211|             raise ValueError(f"Unknown Django op {op_code}")
212| 
213|         return op or node_value

2| This file defines classes for different kinds of nodes of an Abstract
3| Syntax Tree. In general, you will have a different AST node for
4| each kind of grammar rule.
5| 
6| This file has a small bit of metaprogramming to simplify specification
7| and to perform some validation steps.
8| '''
9| 
10| 
11| class AST(object):
12|     _nodes = {}
13| 
14|     @classmethod
15|     def __init_subclass__(cls):
16|         AST._nodes[cls.__name__] = cls
17| 
18|         if not hasattr(cls, '__annotations__'):
19|             return
20| 
21|         cls._fields = list(cls.__annotations__)
22| 
23|     def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
24|         if len(args) != len(self._fields):
25|             raise TypeError(f'{str(self)}: Expected {len(self._fields)} arguments')
26| 
27|         for name, val in zip(self._fields, args):
28|             setattr(self, name, val)
29| 
30|         for name, val in kwargs.items():
31|             setattr(self, name, val)
32| 
33|     def __repr__(self):
34|         parts = []
35| 
36|         for name in self._fields:
37|             val = getattr(self, name)
38| 
39|             if isinstance(val, AST):
40|                 parts.append(f'{name}={type(val).__name__}')
41| 
42|             elif isinstance(val, list):
43|                 parts.append(f'{name}=[ len={len(val)} ]')
44| 
45|             else:
46|                 parts.append(f'{name}={repr(val)}')
47| 
48|         argstr = ', '.join(parts)
49| 
50|         return f'{type(self).__name__}({argstr})'

53| # Specific AST nodes.
54| #

57| # binary operator, you might store the operator, the left expression,

109| # The following classes for visiting and rewriting the AST are taken
110| # from Python's ast module.   It's really easy to make mistakes when
111| # naming methods in visitor classes so there's a bit of metaprogramming
112| # to make sure we're not writing duplicate definitions and to make
113| # sure methods match up with the names of actual AST nodes.
114| 
115| class VisitDict(dict):
116|     def __setitem__(self, key, value):
117|         if key in self:
118|             raise AttributeError(f'Duplicate definition for {key}')
119|         super().__setitem__(key, value)

121| 
122| class NodeVisitMeta(type):
123|     @classmethod
124|     def __prepare__(cls, name, bases):
125|         return VisitDict()

128| class NodeVisitor(metaclass=NodeVisitMeta):
129|     '''
130|     Class for visiting nodes of the parse tree.  This is modeled after
131|     a similar class in the standard library ast.NodeVisitor.  For each
132|     node, the visit(node) method calls a method visit_NodeName(node)
133|     which should be implemented in subclasses.  The generic_visit() method
134|     is called for all nodes where there is no matching visit_NodeName() method.
135| 
136|     Here is a example of a visitor that examines binary operators::
137| 
138|         class VisitOps(NodeVisitor):
139|             visit_BinOp(self,node):
140|                 print('Binary operator', node.op)
141|                 self.visit(node.left)
142|                 self.visit(node.right)
143|             visit_UnaryOp(self,node):
144|                 print('Unary operator', node.op)
145|                 self.visit(node.expr)
146| 
147|         tree = parse(txt)
148|         VisitOps().visit(tree)
149|     '''
150|     def visit(self, node):
151|         '''
152|         Execute a method of the form visit_NodeName(node) where
153|         NodeName is the name of the class of a particular node.
154|         '''
155|         if isinstance(node, list):
156|             for item in node:
157|                 self.visit(item)
158|         elif isinstance(node, AST):
159|             method = 'visit_' + node.__class__.__name__
160|             visitor = getattr(self, method, self.generic_visit)
161|             visitor(node)
162| 
163|     def generic_visit(self, node):
164|         '''
165|         Method executed if no applicable `visit_` method can be found.
166|         This examines the node to see if it has `_fields`, is a list,
167|         or can be further traversed.
168|         '''
169|         for field in getattr(node, '_fields'):
170|             value = getattr(node, field, None)
171|             self.visit(value)

173|     @classmethod
174|     def __init_subclass__(cls):
175|         '''
176|         Sanity check. Make sure that visitor classes use the right names.
177|         '''
178|         for key in vars(cls):
179|             if key.startswith('visit_'):
180|                 assert key[6:] in AST._nodes, f"{key} doesn't match any AST node"

184|     '''
185|     Flatten the entire parse tree into a list for the purposes of
186|     debugging and testing.  This returns a list of tuples of the
187|     form (depth, node) where depth is an integer representing the
188|     parse tree depth and node is the associated AST node.
189|     '''

192|             self.depth = 0
193|             self.nodes = []

2| The logic in this module extracts the path sent in a filter query.
3| 
4| PATCH calls pass a path key-value pair in the payload::
5| 
6|    Valid examples of "path" are as follows:
7| 
8|        "path":"members"
9| 
10|        "path":"name.familyName"
11| 
12|        "path":"addresses[type eq \"work\"]"
13| 
14|        "path":"members[value eq
15|               \"2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646\"]"
16| 
17|        "path":"members[value eq
18|               \"2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646\"].displayName"
19| 
20|                        Figure 8: Example Path Values
21| 
22| Those paths can be simple or complex. The "valuePath" rule allows specific
23| values of a complex multi-valued attribute to be selected::
24| 
25|     RFC 7644, Figure 7: SCIM PATCH PATH Rule, ABNF:
26| 
27|         PATH = attrPath / valuePath [subAttr]
28| 
29| The classes in this module parse the overall PATH string for its parts so
30| that they can be easily used in following code.
31| """
32| import json
33| import string

42|     This class depends on the SQL transpiler.
43|     """
44|     def __init__(self, filter_: str, attr_map: dict):
45|         """
46|         Perform parsing of path.
47|         """
48|         self.filter: str = filter_
49|         self.attr_map: dict = attr_map
50| 
51|         self.token_stream = None
52|         self.ast = None
53|         self.transpiler = None
54| 
55|         self._build()
56| 
57|     def _build(self):
58|         self.token_stream = SCIMLexer().tokenize(self.filter)
59|         self.ast = SCIMParser().parse(self.token_stream)
60|         self.transpiler = Transpiler(self.attr_map)
61|         self.transpiler.transpile(self.ast)
62| 
63|     @property
64|     def is_complex(self) -> bool:
65|         """
66|         Return true if AttrPath has multiple levels within it. Eg::
67| 
68|            "members[value eq "2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646"]"
69| 
70|         The following example is a simple (or not complex) AttrPath::
71| 
72|            "name.familyName"
73|         """
74|         return len(self.transpiler.attr_paths) > 1

34| class Transpiler(ast.NodeTransformer):
35|     """
36|     Transpile a SCIM AST into a Q object
37|     """
38| 
39|     def __init__(self, attr_map: Mapping, *args, **kwargs):
40|         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
41|         self.attr_map = attr_map_with_lower_keys(attr_map)
42| 
43|     def transpile(self, scim_ast) -> (str, dict):
44|         return self.visit(scim_ast)
45| 
46|     def visit_Filter(self, node):
47|         if node.namespace:
48|             # push the namespace from value path down the tree
49|             if isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.Filter):
50|                 node.expr = scim2ast.Filter(
51|                     node.expr.expr, node.expr.negated, node.namespace
52|                 )
53|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.LogExpr):
54|                 expr1 = scim2ast.Filter(
55|                     node.expr.expr1.expr, node.expr.expr1.negated, node.namespace
56|                 )
57|                 expr2 = scim2ast.Filter(
58|                     node.expr.expr2.expr, node.expr.expr2.negated, node.namespace
59|                 )
60|                 node.expr = scim2ast.LogExpr(node.expr.op, expr1, expr2)
61|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.AttrExpr):
62|                 # namespace takes place of previous attr_name in attr_path
63|                 sub_attr = scim2ast.SubAttr(node.expr.attr_path.attr_name)
64|                 attr_path = scim2ast.AttrPath(
65|                     node.namespace.attr_name, sub_attr, node.expr.attr_path.uri
66|                 )
67|                 node.expr = scim2ast.AttrExpr(
68|                     node.expr.value, attr_path, node.expr.comp_value
69|                 )
70|             else:
71|                 raise NotImplementedError(f"Node {node} can not pass on namespace")
72| 
73|         query = self.visit(node.expr)
74| 
75|         if query and node.negated:
76|             query = ~query
77| 
78|         return query
79| 
80|     def visit_LogExpr(self, node):
81|         q1 = self.visit(node.expr1)
82|         q2 = self.visit(node.expr2)
83|         op = node.op.upper()
84|         if q1 and q2:
85|             if op == "AND":
86|                 return q1 & q2
87|             elif op == "OR":
88|                 return q1 | q2
89|         elif q1:
90|             return q1
91|         elif q2:
92|             return q2
93|         else:
94|             return None
95| 
96|     def visit_PartialAttrExpr(self, node):
97|         """
98|         Dissect rather complex queries like the following::
99| 
100|             emails[type eq "Primary"].value eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
101| 
102|         First we restructure to something like this::
103| 
104|             emails.value[type eq "Primary"] eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
105| 
106|         Then we get SQL like this 'emails.type = {0}' and 'emails.value'.
107| 
108|         We need to take these two snippets and AND them together.
109|         """
110|         # visit full filter first and restructure AST
111|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.type = {0}'
112|         full = self.visit(node)
113| 
114|         # get second part of query
115|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.value'
116|         partial = self.visit(node.namespace)
117|         return full, partial
118| 
119|     def is_filter(self, node):
120|         full, partial = self.visit_PartialAttrExpr(node.attr_path.attr_name)
121|         if partial and "." in partial:
122|             partial = partial.replace(".", "__")
123|         if full and partial:
124|             # Specific to Azure
125|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
126|             key = partial + "__" + op
127|             return full & Q(**{key: value})
128|         elif full:
129|             return full
130|         elif partial:
131|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
132|             key = partial + "__" + op
133|             return Q(**{key: value})
134|         else:
135|             return None
136| 
137|     def visit_AttrExpr(self, node):
138|         if isinstance(node.attr_path.attr_name, scim2ast.Filter):
139|             return self.is_filter(node)
140|         attr = self.visit(node.attr_path)
141|         if attr is None:
142|             return None
143|         if "." in attr:
144|             attr = attr.replace(".", "__")
145|         op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
146|         key = attr + "__" + op
147|         query = Q(**{key: value})
148|         if node.value == "ne":
149|             query = ~query
150|         return query
151| 
152|     def visit_AttrExprValue(self, node_value, node_comp_value):
153|         op = self.lookup_op(node_value)
154| 
155|         if node_comp_value:
156|             # There is a comp_value, so visit node and build SQL.
157|             # prep item_id to be a str replacement placeholder
158|             value = self.visit(node_comp_value)
159|         else:
160|             value = None
161| 
162|         if op == "isnull":  # __isnull=False
163|             value = False
164| 
165|         return op, value
166| 
167|     def visit_AttrPath(self, node):
168|         attr_name_value = node.attr_name.lower()
169|         sub_attr_value = None
170|         if node.sub_attr:
171|             sub_attr_value = node.sub_attr.value.lower()
172| 
173|         uri_value = None
174|         if node.uri:

176| 
177|         # Convert attr_name to another value based on map.
178|         # Otherwise, return None.
179|         attr_path_tuple = (attr_name_value, sub_attr_value, uri_value)
180|         return self.attr_map.get(attr_path_tuple)
181| 
182|     @staticmethod
183|     def visit_CompValue(node):
184|         if node.value == "true":
185|             return True
186|         elif node.value == "false":
187|             return False
188|         elif node.value == "null":
189|             return None
190|         else:
191|             return node.value

208|         }.get(op_code)

210|         if not op:
211|             raise ValueError(f"Unknown Django op {op_code}")

2| This file defines classes for different kinds of nodes of an Abstract
3| Syntax Tree. In general, you will have a different AST node for
4| each kind of grammar rule.
5| 
6| This file has a small bit of metaprogramming to simplify specification
7| and to perform some validation steps.
8| '''
9| 
10| 
11| class AST(object):
12|     _nodes = {}
13| 
14|     @classmethod
15|     def __init_subclass__(cls):
16|         AST._nodes[cls.__name__] = cls
17| 
18|         if not hasattr(cls, '__annotations__'):
19|             return
20| 
21|         cls._fields = list(cls.__annotations__)
22| 
23|     def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
24|         if len(args) != len(self._fields):
25|             raise TypeError(f'{str(self)}: Expected {len(self._fields)} arguments')
26| 
27|         for name, val in zip(self._fields, args):
28|             setattr(self, name, val)
29| 
30|         for name, val in kwargs.items():
31|             setattr(self, name, val)
32| 
33|     def __repr__(self):
34|         parts = []
35| 
36|         for name in self._fields:
37|             val = getattr(self, name)
38| 
39|             if isinstance(val, AST):
40|                 parts.append(f'{name}={type(val).__name__}')
41| 
42|             elif isinstance(val, list):
43|                 parts.append(f'{name}=[ len={len(val)} ]')
44| 
45|             else:
46|                 parts.append(f'{name}={repr(val)}')
47| 
48|         argstr = ', '.join(parts)
49| 
50|         return f'{type(self).__name__}({argstr})'

53| # Specific AST nodes.
54| #

57| # binary operator, you might store the operator, the left expression,

109| # The following classes for visiting and rewriting the AST are taken
110| # from Python's ast module.   It's really easy to make mistakes when
111| # naming methods in visitor classes so there's a bit of metaprogramming
112| # to make sure we're not writing duplicate definitions and to make
113| # sure methods match up with the names of actual AST nodes.
114| 
115| class VisitDict(dict):
116|     def __setitem__(self, key, value):
117|         if key in self:
118|             raise AttributeError(f'Duplicate definition for {key}')
119|         super().__setitem__(key, value)

121| 
122| class NodeVisitMeta(type):
123|     @classmethod
124|     def __prepare__(cls, name, bases):
125|         return VisitDict()

128| class NodeVisitor(metaclass=NodeVisitMeta):
129|     '''
130|     Class for visiting nodes of the parse tree.  This is modeled after
131|     a similar class in the standard library ast.NodeVisitor.  For each
132|     node, the visit(node) method calls a method visit_NodeName(node)
133|     which should be implemented in subclasses.  The generic_visit() method
134|     is called for all nodes where there is no matching visit_NodeName() method.
135| 
136|     Here is a example of a visitor that examines binary operators::
137| 
138|         class VisitOps(NodeVisitor):
139|             visit_BinOp(self,node):
140|                 print('Binary operator', node.op)
141|                 self.visit(node.left)
142|                 self.visit(node.right)
143|             visit_UnaryOp(self,node):
144|                 print('Unary operator', node.op)
145|                 self.visit(node.expr)
146| 
147|         tree = parse(txt)
148|         VisitOps().visit(tree)
149|     '''
150|     def visit(self, node):
151|         '''
152|         Execute a method of the form visit_NodeName(node) where
153|         NodeName is the name of the class of a particular node.
154|         '''
155|         if isinstance(node, list):
156|             for item in node:
157|                 self.visit(item)
158|         elif isinstance(node, AST):
159|             method = 'visit_' + node.__class__.__name__
160|             visitor = getattr(self, method, self.generic_visit)
161|             visitor(node)
162| 
163|     def generic_visit(self, node):
164|         '''
165|         Method executed if no applicable `visit_` method can be found.
166|         This examines the node to see if it has `_fields`, is a list,
167|         or can be further traversed.
168|         '''
169|         for field in getattr(node, '_fields'):
170|             value = getattr(node, field, None)
171|             self.visit(value)

173|     @classmethod
174|     def __init_subclass__(cls):
175|         '''
176|         Sanity check. Make sure that visitor classes use the right names.
177|         '''
178|         for key in vars(cls):
179|             if key.startswith('visit_'):
180|                 assert key[6:] in AST._nodes, f"{key} doesn't match any AST node"

184|     '''
185|     Flatten the entire parse tree into a list for the purposes of
186|     debugging and testing.  This returns a list of tuples of the
187|     form (depth, node) where depth is an integer representing the
188|     parse tree depth and node is the associated AST node.
189|     '''

192|             self.depth = 0
193|             self.nodes = []

2| The logic in this module extracts the path sent in a filter query.
3| 
4| PATCH calls pass a path key-value pair in the payload::
5| 
6|    Valid examples of "path" are as follows:
7| 
8|        "path":"members"
9| 
10|        "path":"name.familyName"
11| 
12|        "path":"addresses[type eq \"work\"]"
13| 
14|        "path":"members[value eq
15|               \"2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646\"]"
16| 
17|        "path":"members[value eq
18|               \"2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646\"].displayName"
19| 
20|                        Figure 8: Example Path Values
21| 
22| Those paths can be simple or complex. The "valuePath" rule allows specific
23| values of a complex multi-valued attribute to be selected::
24| 
25|     RFC 7644, Figure 7: SCIM PATCH PATH Rule, ABNF:
26| 
27|         PATH = attrPath / valuePath [subAttr]
28| 
29| The classes in this module parse the overall PATH string for its parts so
30| that they can be easily used in following code.
31| """
32| import json
33| import string

42|     This class depends on the SQL transpiler.
43|     """
44|     def __init__(self, filter_: str, attr_map: dict):
45|         """
46|         Perform parsing of path.
47|         """
48|         self.filter: str = filter_
49|         self.attr_map: dict = attr_map
50| 
51|         self.token_stream = None
52|         self.ast = None
53|         self.transpiler = None
54| 
55|         self._build()
56| 
57|     def _build(self):
58|         self.token_stream = SCIMLexer().tokenize(self.filter)
59|         self.ast = SCIMParser().parse(self.token_stream)
60|         self.transpiler = Transpiler(self.attr_map)
61|         self.transpiler.transpile(self.ast)
62| 
63|     @property
64|     def is_complex(self) -> bool:
65|         """
66|         Return true if AttrPath has multiple levels within it. Eg::
67| 
68|            "members[value eq "2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646"]"
69| 
70|         The following example is a simple (or not complex) AttrPath::
71| 
72|            "name.familyName"
73|         """
74|         return len(self.transpiler.attr_paths) > 1

34| class Transpiler(ast.NodeTransformer):
35|     """
36|     Transpile a SCIM AST into a Q object
37|     """
38| 
39|     def __init__(self, attr_map: Mapping, *args, **kwargs):
40|         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
41|         self.attr_map = attr_map_with_lower_keys(attr_map)
42| 
43|     def transpile(self, scim_ast) -> (str, dict):
44|         return self.visit(scim_ast)
45| 
46|     def visit_Filter(self, node):
47|         if node.namespace:
48|             # push the namespace from value path down the tree
49|             if isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.Filter):
50|                 node.expr = scim2ast.Filter(
51|                     node.expr.expr, node.expr.negated, node.namespace
52|                 )
53|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.LogExpr):
54|                 expr1 = scim2ast.Filter(
55|                     node.expr.expr1.expr, node.expr.expr1.negated, node.namespace
56|                 )
57|                 expr2 = scim2ast.Filter(
58|                     node.expr.expr2.expr, node.expr.expr2.negated, node.namespace
59|                 )
60|                 node.expr = scim2ast.LogExpr(node.expr.op, expr1, expr2)
61|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.AttrExpr):
62|                 # namespace takes place of previous attr_name in attr_path
63|                 sub_attr = scim2ast.SubAttr(node.expr.attr_path.attr_name)
64|                 attr_path = scim2ast.AttrPath(
65|                     node.namespace.attr_name, sub_attr, node.expr.attr_path.uri
66|                 )
67|                 node.expr = scim2ast.AttrExpr(
68|                     node.expr.value, attr_path, node.expr.comp_value
69|                 )
70|             else:
71|                 raise NotImplementedError(f"Node {node} can not pass on namespace")
72| 
73|         query = self.visit(node.expr)
74| 
75|         if query and node.negated:
76|             query = ~query
77| 
78|         return query
79| 
80|     def visit_LogExpr(self, node):
81|         q1 = self.visit(node.expr1)
82|         q2 = self.visit(node.expr2)
83|         op = node.op.upper()
84|         if q1 and q2:
85|             if op == "AND":
86|                 return q1 & q2
87|             elif op == "OR":
88|                 return q1 | q2
89|         elif q1:
90|             return q1
91|         elif q2:
92|             return q2
93|         else:
94|             return None
95| 
96|     def visit_PartialAttrExpr(self, node):
97|         """
98|         Dissect rather complex queries like the following::
99| 
100|             emails[type eq "Primary"].value eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
101| 
102|         First we restructure to something like this::
103| 
104|             emails.value[type eq "Primary"] eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
105| 
106|         Then we get SQL like this 'emails.type = {0}' and 'emails.value'.
107| 
108|         We need to take these two snippets and AND them together.
109|         """
110|         # visit full filter first and restructure AST
111|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.type = {0}'
112|         full = self.visit(node)
113| 
114|         # get second part of query
115|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.value'
116|         partial = self.visit(node.namespace)
117|         return full, partial
118| 
119|     def is_filter(self, node):
120|         full, partial = self.visit_PartialAttrExpr(node.attr_path.attr_name)
121|         if partial and "." in partial:
122|             partial = partial.replace(".", "__")
123|         if full and partial:
124|             # Specific to Azure
125|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
126|             key = partial + "__" + op
127|             return full & Q(**{key: value})
128|         elif full:
129|             return full
130|         elif partial:
131|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
132|             key = partial + "__" + op
133|             return Q(**{key: value})
134|         else:
135|             return None
136| 
137|     def visit_AttrExpr(self, node):
138|         if isinstance(node.attr_path.attr_name, scim2ast.Filter):
139|             return self.is_filter(node)
140|         attr = self.visit(node.attr_path)
141|         if attr is None:
142|             return None
143|         if "." in attr:
144|             attr = attr.replace(".", "__")
145|         op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
146|         key = attr + "__" + op
147|         query = Q(**{key: value})
148|         if node.value == "ne":
149|             query = ~query
150|         return query
151| 
152|     def visit_AttrExprValue(self, node_value, node_comp_value):
153|         op = self.lookup_op(node_value)
154| 
155|         if node_comp_value:
156|             # There is a comp_value, so visit node and build SQL.
157|             # prep item_id to be a str replacement placeholder
158|             value = self.visit(node_comp_value)
159|         else:
160|             value = None
161| 
162|         if op == "isnull":  # __isnull=False
163|             value = False
164| 
165|         return op, value
166| 
167|     def visit_AttrPath(self, node):
168|         attr_name_value = node.attr_name.lower()
169|         sub_attr_value = None
170|         if node.sub_attr:
171|             sub_attr_value = node.sub_attr.value.lower()
172| 
173|         uri_value = None
174|         if node.uri:

176| 
177|         # Convert attr_name to another value based on map.
178|         # Otherwise, return None.
179|         attr_path_tuple = (attr_name_value, sub_attr_value, uri_value)
180|         return self.attr_map.get(attr_path_tuple)
181| 
182|     @staticmethod
183|     def visit_CompValue(node):
184|         if node.value == "true":
185|             return True
186|         elif node.value == "false":
187|             return False
188|         elif node.value == "null":
189|             return None
190|         else:
191|             return node.value

208|         }.get(op_code)

210|         if not op:
211|             raise ValueError(f"Unknown Django op {op_code}")

34| class Transpiler(ast.NodeTransformer):
35|     """
36|     Transpile a SCIM AST into a Q object
37|     """

39|     def __init__(self, attr_map: Mapping, *args, **kwargs):
40|         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
41|         self.attr_map = attr_map_with_lower_keys(attr_map)

44|         return self.visit(scim_ast)

46|     def visit_Filter(self, node):
47|         if node.namespace:
48|             # push the namespace from value path down the tree
49|             if isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.Filter):
50|                 node.expr = scim2ast.Filter(
51|                     node.expr.expr, node.expr.negated, node.namespace
52|                 )
53|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.LogExpr):
54|                 expr1 = scim2ast.Filter(
55|                     node.expr.expr1.expr, node.expr.expr1.negated, node.namespace
56|                 )
57|                 expr2 = scim2ast.Filter(
58|                     node.expr.expr2.expr, node.expr.expr2.negated, node.namespace
59|                 )
60|                 node.expr = scim2ast.LogExpr(node.expr.op, expr1, expr2)
61|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.AttrExpr):
62|                 # namespace takes place of previous attr_name in attr_path
63|                 sub_attr = scim2ast.SubAttr(node.expr.attr_path.attr_name)
64|                 attr_path = scim2ast.AttrPath(
65|                     node.namespace.attr_name, sub_attr, node.expr.attr_path.uri
66|                 )
67|                 node.expr = scim2ast.AttrExpr(
68|                     node.expr.value, attr_path, node.expr.comp_value
69|                 )
70|             else:
71|                 raise NotImplementedError(f"Node {node} can not pass on namespace")
72| 
73|         query = self.visit(node.expr)
74| 
75|         if query and node.negated:
76|             query = ~query
77| 
78|         return query
79| 
80|     def visit_LogExpr(self, node):
81|         q1 = self.visit(node.expr1)
82|         q2 = self.visit(node.expr2)
83|         op = node.op.upper()
84|         if q1 and q2:
85|             if op == "AND":
86|                 return q1 & q2
87|             elif op == "OR":
88|                 return q1 | q2
89|         elif q1:
90|             return q1
91|         elif q2:
92|             return q2
93|         else:
94|             return None
95| 
96|     def visit_PartialAttrExpr(self, node):
97|         """
98|         Dissect rather complex queries like the following::
99| 
100|             emails[type eq "Primary"].value eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
101| 
102|         First we restructure to something like this::
103| 
104|             emails.value[type eq "Primary"] eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
105| 
106|         Then we get SQL like this 'emails.type = {0}' and 'emails.value'.
107| 
108|         We need to take these two snippets and AND them together.
109|         """
110|         # visit full filter first and restructure AST
111|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.type = {0}'
112|         full = self.visit(node)
113| 
114|         # get second part of query
115|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.value'
116|         partial = self.visit(node.namespace)
117|         return full, partial
118| 
119|     def is_filter(self, node):
120|         full, partial = self.visit_PartialAttrExpr(node.attr_path.attr_name)
121|         if partial and "." in partial:
122|             partial = partial.replace(".", "__")
123|         if full and partial:
124|             # Specific to Azure
125|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
126|             key = partial + "__" + op
127|             return full & Q(**{key: value})
128|         elif full:
129|             return full
130|         elif partial:
131|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
132|             key = partial + "__" + op
133|             return Q(**{key: value})
134|         else:
135|             return None
136| 
137|     def visit_AttrExpr(self, node):
138|         if isinstance(node.attr_path.attr_name, scim2ast.Filter):
139|             return self.is_filter(node)
140|         attr = self.visit(node.attr_path)
141|         if attr is None:
142|             return None
143|         if "." in attr:
144|             attr = attr.replace(".", "__")
145|         op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
146|         key = attr + "__" + op
147|         query = Q(**{key: value})
148|         if node.value == "ne":
149|             query = ~query
150|         return query
151| 
152|     def visit_AttrExprValue(self, node_value, node_comp_value):
153|         op = self.lookup_op(node_value)
154| 
155|         if node_comp_value:
156|             # There is a comp_value, so visit node and build SQL.
157|             # prep item_id to be a str replacement placeholder
158|             value = self.visit(node_comp_value)

161| 
162|         if op == "isnull":  # __isnull=False
163|             value = False

165|         return op, value

167|     def visit_AttrPath(self, node):

169|         sub_attr_value = None

5| 
6|    Valid examples of "path" are as follows:
7| 
8|        "path":"members"
9| 
10|        "path":"name.familyName"
11|

19|

23| values of a complex multi-valued attribute to be selected::
24| 
25|     RFC 7644, Figure 7: SCIM PATCH PATH Rule, ABNF:
26| 
27|         PATH = attrPath / valuePath [subAttr]
28| 
29| The classes in this module parse the overall PATH string for its parts so
30| that they can be easily used in following code.

2| The logic in this module builds a Django Q object from an SCIM filter.
3| """
4| import ast
5| from typing import Mapping
6| 
7| from django.db.models import Q
8| 
9| from scim2_filter_parser import ast as scim2ast
10| from scim2_filter_parser.lexer import SCIMLexer
11| from scim2_filter_parser.parser import SCIMParser
12| 
13| 
14| def get_query(scim_query: str, attr_map: Mapping):
15|     token_stream = SCIMLexer().tokenize(scim_query)
16|     tree = SCIMParser().parse(token_stream)
17|     return Transpiler(attr_map).transpile(tree)
18| 
19| 
20| def attr_map_with_lower_keys(attr_map: Mapping) -> Mapping:
21|     attr_map_lower_case = {}
22|     for (a, b, c), v in attr_map.items():
23|         if a:
24|             a = a.lower()
25|         if b:
26|             b = b.lower()
27|         if c:
28|             c = c.lower()
29|         attr_map_lower_case[(a, b, c)] = v
30|     return attr_map_lower_case
31| 
32| 
33| # noinspection PyPep8Naming
34| class Transpiler(ast.NodeTransformer):
35|     """
36|     Transpile a SCIM AST into a Q object
37|     """
38| 
39|     def __init__(self, attr_map: Mapping, *args, **kwargs):
40|         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
41|         self.attr_map = attr_map_with_lower_keys(attr_map)
42| 
43|     def transpile(self, scim_ast) -> (str, dict):
44|         return self.visit(scim_ast)
45| 
46|     def visit_Filter(self, node):
47|         if node.namespace:
48|             # push the namespace from value path down the tree
49|             if isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.Filter):
50|                 node.expr = scim2ast.Filter(
51|                     node.expr.expr, node.expr.negated, node.namespace
52|                 )
53|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.LogExpr):
54|                 expr1 = scim2ast.Filter(
55|                     node.expr.expr1.expr, node.expr.expr1.negated, node.namespace
56|                 )
57|                 expr2 = scim2ast.Filter(
58|                     node.expr.expr2.expr, node.expr.expr2.negated, node.namespace
59|                 )
60|                 node.expr = scim2ast.LogExpr(node.expr.op, expr1, expr2)
61|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.AttrExpr):
62|                 # namespace takes place of previous attr_name in attr_path
63|                 sub_attr = scim2ast.SubAttr(node.expr.attr_path.attr_name)
64|                 attr_path = scim2ast.AttrPath(
65|                     node.namespace.attr_name, sub_attr, node.expr.attr_path.uri
66|                 )
67|                 node.expr = scim2ast.AttrExpr(
68|                     node.expr.value, attr_path, node.expr.comp_value
69|                 )
70|             else:
71|                 raise NotImplementedError(f"Node {node} can not pass on namespace")
72| 
73|         query = self.visit(node.expr)
74| 
75|         if query and node.negated:
76|             query = ~query
77| 
78|         return query
79| 
80|     def visit_LogExpr(self, node):
81|         q1 = self.visit(node.expr1)
82|         q2 = self.visit(node.expr2)
83|         op = node.op.upper()
84|         if q1 and q2:
85|             if op == "AND":
86|                 return q1 & q2
87|             elif op == "OR":
88|                 return q1 | q2
89|         elif q1:
90|             return q1
91|         elif q2:
92|             return q2
93|         else:
94|             return None
95| 
96|     def visit_PartialAttrExpr(self, node):
97|         """
98|         Dissect rather complex queries like the following::
99| 
100|             emails[type eq "Primary"].value eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
101| 
102|         First we restructure to something like this::
103| 
104|             emails.value[type eq "Primary"] eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
105| 
106|         Then we get SQL like this 'emails.type = {0}' and 'emails.value'.
107| 
108|         We need to take these two snippets and AND them together.
109|         """
110|         # visit full filter first and restructure AST
111|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.type = {0}'
112|         full = self.visit(node)
113| 
114|         # get second part of query
115|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.value'
116|         partial = self.visit(node.namespace)
117|         return full, partial
118| 
119|     def is_filter(self, node):
120|         full, partial = self.visit_PartialAttrExpr(node.attr_path.attr_name)
121|         if partial and "." in partial:
122|             partial = partial.replace(".", "__")
123|         if full and partial:
124|             # Specific to Azure
125|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
126|             key = partial + "__" + op
127|             return full & Q(**{key: value})
128|         elif full:
129|             return full
130|         elif partial:
131|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
132|             key = partial + "__" + op
133|             return Q(**{key: value})
134|         else:
135|             return None
136| 
137|     def visit_AttrExpr(self, node):
138|         if isinstance(node.attr_path.attr_name, scim2ast.Filter):
139|             return self.is_filter(node)
140|         attr = self.visit(node.attr_path)
141|         if attr is None:
142|             return None
143|         if "." in attr:
144|             attr = attr.replace(".", "__")
145|         op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
146|         key = attr + "__" + op
147|         query = Q(**{key: value})
148|         if node.value == "ne":
149|             query = ~query
150|         return query
151| 
152|     def visit_AttrExprValue(self, node_value, node_comp_value):
153|         op = self.lookup_op(node_value)
154| 
155|         if node_comp_value:
156|             # There is a comp_value, so visit node and build SQL.
157|             # prep item_id to be a str replacement placeholder
158|             value = self.visit(node_comp_value)
159|         else:
160|             value = None
161| 
162|         if op == "isnull":  # __isnull=False
163|             value = False
164| 
165|         return op, value
166| 
167|     def visit_AttrPath(self, node):
168|         attr_name_value = node.attr_name.lower()
169|         sub_attr_value = None
170|         if node.sub_attr:
171|             sub_attr_value = node.sub_attr.value.lower()
172| 
173|         uri_value = None
174|         if node.uri:
175|             uri_value = node.uri.lower()
176| 
177|         # Convert attr_name to another value based on map.
178|         # Otherwise, return None.
179|         attr_path_tuple = (attr_name_value, sub_attr_value, uri_value)
180|         return self.attr_map.get(attr_path_tuple)
181| 
182|     @staticmethod
183|     def visit_CompValue(node):
184|         if node.value == "true":
185|             return True
186|         elif node.value == "false":
187|             return False
188|         elif node.value == "null":
189|             return None
190|         else:
191|             return node.value
192| 
193|     @staticmethod
194|     def lookup_op(node_value):
195|         op_code = node_value.lower()
196| 
197|         op = {
198|             "eq": "iexact",
199|             "ne": "iexact",
200|             "co": "icontains",
201|             "sw": "istartswith",
202|             "ew": "iendswith",
203|             "pr": "isnull",
204|             "gt": "gt",
205|             "ge": "gte",
206|             "lt": "lt",
207|             "le": "lte",
208|         }.get(op_code)
209| 
210|         if not op:
211|             raise ValueError(f"Unknown Django op {op_code}")
212| 
213|         return op or node_value

3| 
4| PATCH calls pass a path key-value pair in the payload::
5| 
6|    Valid examples of "path" are as follows:
7| 
8|        "path":"members"
9| 
10|        "path":"name.familyName"
11| 
12|        "path":"addresses[type eq \"work\"]"
13| 
14|        "path":"members[value eq

17|        "path":"members[value eq
18|               \"2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646\"].displayName"
19| 
20|                        Figure 8: Example Path Values
21| 
22| Those paths can be simple or complex. The "valuePath" rule allows specific
23| values of a complex multi-valued attribute to be selected::
24| 
25|     RFC 7644, Figure 7: SCIM PATCH PATH Rule, ABNF:
26| 
27|         PATH = attrPath / valuePath [subAttr]
28| 
29| The classes in this module parse the overall PATH string for its parts so
30| that they can be easily used in following code.
31| """
32| import json

60|         self.transpiler = Transpiler(self.attr_map)

1| """
2| The logic in this module builds a Django Q object from an SCIM filter.
3| """
4| import ast
5| from typing import Mapping
6| 
7| from django.db.models import Q
8| 
9| from scim2_filter_parser import ast as scim2ast
10| from scim2_filter_parser.lexer import SCIMLexer
11| from scim2_filter_parser.parser import SCIMParser
12| 
13| 
14| def get_query(scim_query: str, attr_map: Mapping):
15|     token_stream = SCIMLexer().tokenize(scim_query)
16|     tree = SCIMParser().parse(token_stream)
17|     return Transpiler(attr_map).transpile(tree)
18| 
19| 
20| def attr_map_with_lower_keys(attr_map: Mapping) -> Mapping:
21|     attr_map_lower_case = {}
22|     for (a, b, c), v in attr_map.items():
23|         if a:
24|             a = a.lower()
25|         if b:
26|             b = b.lower()
27|         if c:
28|             c = c.lower()
29|         attr_map_lower_case[(a, b, c)] = v
30|     return attr_map_lower_case
31| 
32| 
33| # noinspection PyPep8Naming
34| class Transpiler(ast.NodeTransformer):
35|     """
36|     Transpile a SCIM AST into a Q object
37|     """
38| 
39|     def __init__(self, attr_map: Mapping, *args, **kwargs):
40|         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
41|         self.attr_map = attr_map_with_lower_keys(attr_map)
42| 
43|     def transpile(self, scim_ast) -> (str, dict):
44|         return self.visit(scim_ast)
45| 
46|     def visit_Filter(self, node):
47|         if node.namespace:
48|             # push the namespace from value path down the tree
49|             if isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.Filter):
50|                 node.expr = scim2ast.Filter(
51|                     node.expr.expr, node.expr.negated, node.namespace
52|                 )
53|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.LogExpr):
54|                 expr1 = scim2ast.Filter(
55|                     node.expr.expr1.expr, node.expr.expr1.negated, node.namespace
56|                 )
57|                 expr2 = scim2ast.Filter(
58|                     node.expr.expr2.expr, node.expr.expr2.negated, node.namespace
59|                 )
60|                 node.expr = scim2ast.LogExpr(node.expr.op, expr1, expr2)
61|             elif isinstance(node.expr, scim2ast.AttrExpr):
62|                 # namespace takes place of previous attr_name in attr_path
63|                 sub_attr = scim2ast.SubAttr(node.expr.attr_path.attr_name)
64|                 attr_path = scim2ast.AttrPath(
65|                     node.namespace.attr_name, sub_attr, node.expr.attr_path.uri
66|                 )
67|                 node.expr = scim2ast.AttrExpr(
68|                     node.expr.value, attr_path, node.expr.comp_value
69|                 )
70|             else:
71|                 raise NotImplementedError(f"Node {node} can not pass on namespace")
72| 
73|         query = self.visit(node.expr)
74| 
75|         if query and node.negated:
76|             query = ~query
77| 
78|         return query
79| 
80|     def visit_LogExpr(self, node):
81|         q1 = self.visit(node.expr1)
82|         q2 = self.visit(node.expr2)
83|         op = node.op.upper()
84|         if q1 and q2:
85|             if op == "AND":
86|                 return q1 & q2
87|             elif op == "OR":
88|                 return q1 | q2
89|         elif q1:
90|             return q1
91|         elif q2:
92|             return q2
93|         else:
94|             return None
95| 
96|     def visit_PartialAttrExpr(self, node):
97|         """
98|         Dissect rather complex queries like the following::
99| 
100|             emails[type eq "Primary"].value eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
101| 
102|         First we restructure to something like this::
103| 
104|             emails.value[type eq "Primary"] eq "001750ca-8202-47cd-b553-c63f4f245940"
105| 
106|         Then we get SQL like this 'emails.type = {0}' and 'emails.value'.
107| 
108|         We need to take these two snippets and AND them together.
109|         """
110|         # visit full filter first and restructure AST
111|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.type = {0}'
112|         full = self.visit(node)
113| 
114|         # get second part of query
115|         # ie. visit -> 'emails.value'
116|         partial = self.visit(node.namespace)
117|         return full, partial
118| 
119|     def is_filter(self, node):
120|         full, partial = self.visit_PartialAttrExpr(node.attr_path.attr_name)
121|         if partial and "." in partial:
122|             partial = partial.replace(".", "__")
123|         if full and partial:
124|             # Specific to Azure
125|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
126|             key = partial + "__" + op
127|             return full & Q(**{key: value})
128|         elif full:
129|             return full
130|         elif partial:
131|             op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
132|             key = partial + "__" + op
133|             return Q(**{key: value})
134|         else:
135|             return None
136| 
137|     def visit_AttrExpr(self, node):
138|         if isinstance(node.attr_path.attr_name, scim2ast.Filter):
139|             return self.is_filter(node)
140|         attr = self.visit(node.attr_path)
141|         if attr is None:
142|             return None
143|         if "." in attr:
144|             attr = attr.replace(".", "__")
145|         op, value = self.visit_AttrExprValue(node.value, node.comp_value)
146|         key = attr + "__" + op
147|         query = Q(**{key: value})
148|         if node.value == "ne":
149|             query = ~query
150|         return query
151| 
152|     def visit_AttrExprValue(self, node_value, node_comp_value):
153|         op = self.lookup_op(node_value)
154| 
155|         if node_comp_value:
156|             # There is a comp_value, so visit node and build SQL.
157|             # prep item_id to be a str replacement placeholder
158|             value = self.visit(node_comp_value)
159|         else:
160|             value = None
161| 
162|         if op == "isnull":  # __isnull=False
163|             value = False
164| 
165|         return op, value
166| 
167|     def visit_AttrPath(self, node):
168|         attr_name_value = node.attr_name.lower()
169|         sub_attr_value = None
170|         if node.sub_attr:
171|             sub_attr_value = node.sub_attr.value.lower()
172| 
173|         uri_value = None
174|         if node.uri:
175|             uri_value = node.uri.lower()
176| 
177|         # Convert attr_name to another value based on map.
178|         # Otherwise, return None.
179|         attr_path_tuple = (attr_name_value, sub_attr_value, uri_value)
180|         return self.attr_map.get(attr_path_tuple)
181| 
182|     @staticmethod
183|     def visit_CompValue(node):
184|         if node.value == "true":
185|             return True
186|         elif node.value == "false":
187|             return False
188|         elif node.value == "null":
189|             return None
190|         else:
191|             return node.value
192| 
193|     @staticmethod
194|     def lookup_op(node_value):
195|         op_code = node_value.lower()
196| 
197|         op = {
198|             "eq": "iexact",
199|             "ne": "iexact",
200|             "co": "icontains",
201|             "sw": "istartswith",
202|             "ew": "iendswith",
203|             "pr": "isnull",
204|             "gt": "gt",
205|             "ge": "gte",
206|             "lt": "lt",
207|             "le": "lte",
208|         }.get(op_code)
209| 
210|         if not op:
211|             raise ValueError(f"Unknown Django op {op_code}")
212| 
213|         return op or node_value

11| class Transpiler(ast.NodeTransformer):
12|     """
13|     Transpile a SCIM AST into a SQL WHERE clause (not including the "WHERE" keyword)
14|     """
15| 
16|     def __init__(self, attr_map, *args, **kwargs):
17|         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
18| 
19|         self.attr_map = attr_map
20|         self.params = {}
21|         self.attr_paths = []
